channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Implement "Barnahus" System for Child Victims of Violence
item.description: Uzbekistan is planning to implement the "Barnahus" system, a child-centered model for working with children who are victims or witnesses of violence. The system aims to prevent children from repeatedly recounting traumatic experiences to different institutions. This coordinated approach, first developed in Iceland, creates a safe and comfortable environment for children.

item.title: Tashkent to Temporarily Suspend Hot Water Supply from September 14 for Maintenance
item.description: Tashkent will temporarily suspend hot water supply starting September 14 for planned maintenance of heating networks and boiler houses. This is part of preparations for the autumn-winter season to ensure uninterrupted heating for residents. Planned 5-day interruptions in hot water supply will occur throughout September and October.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President urges branches of power to strengthen inter-branch cooperation
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov stated that Kyrgyzstan can only progress when the executive, legislative, and presidential branches of power cooperate constructively. He emphasized that while differences of opinion are natural, state and public interests must be paramount. Japarov highlighted recent economic growth and infrastructure development.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan MP criticizes poor quality asphalt laid in Bishkek
item.description: A member of the Kyrgyz parliament has criticized the quality of asphalt being laid in Bishkek, stating it loses shape quickly like plasticine. He warned this poses risks to public safety and increases the likelihood of traffic accidents. The MP also called for an investigation into the fuel quality in the capital.

item.title: Malik Bekturganov approved as Kyrgyzstan's Prosecutor General
item.description: The Parliament of Kyrgyzstan has approved Malik Bekturganov as the new Prosecutor General. Bekturganov, born in 1974, graduated with a law degree and has held various prosecutorial positions since 1998, including acting Prosecutor General. He previously worked in Bishkek's prosecutor's office and the Prosecutor General's Office.

item.title: Uzbekistan's GDP per capita growing faster than Kazakhstan's, but gap widens
item.description: Uzbekistan's GDP per capita is growing faster than Kazakhstan's, but the gap between the two countries is widening, according to a World Bank report. Over the past 20 years, this indicator has increased fivefold in Kazakhstan and sevenfold in Uzbekistan. Despite faster growth, the disparity is increasing.

item.title: Who will participate in Kyrgyzstan's 2027 presidential election?
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will elect its president on January 27, 2027. Incumbent Sadyr Japarov has stated his intention to run for a second term, noting no restrictions for potential candidates. Former deputy Ishak Masaliev expressed uncertainty about his candidacy, emphasizing the need for resources and fair electoral processes.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's international standing has improved, says President Saparov
item.description: President Saparov stated that hosting major international events has boosted Kyrgyzstan's global reputation and strengthened its position. Recent events include the SCO summit, the SCO+ meeting, state visits by China's Xi Jinping and Pakistan's PM Sharif, and the World Nomad Games. Kyrgyzstan's upcoming SCO presidency in 2025-2026 is a significant diplomatic milestone.

item.title: Kyrgyz Parliament approves two new ministerial appointments
item.description: The Kyrgyz Parliament has approved Almaz Imangaziev as Minister of Labor, Social Security, and Migration, and Almaz Aiylchiev as Minister of Justice. Imangaziev, a career diplomat, previously served as deputy foreign minister. Aiylchiev held positions within the Presidential Administration's Legal Support Department. MPs urged the new labor minister to focus on employment for disabled individuals and review poverty allowance allocation.

item.title: Fourteen individuals detained in Tashkent suspected of involvement in transnational drug network
item.description: Fourteen people have been detained in Tashkent on suspicion of involvement in a transnational criminal organization. The detentions occurred during coordinated operations across several districts, involving multiple law enforcement agencies and international cooperation. A university student was found with synthetic drugs while working as an online drug courier. The operation dismantled interconnected links of the drug network.

item.title: Russia may intensify attacks on Ukraine infrastructure this winter, Bloomberg reports
item.description: Russia intends to increase its attacks on Ukraine's energy and heating infrastructure during the winter, according to Bloomberg, citing European officials. The report suggests Russia may also escalate hybrid attacks and political interference in Europe to weaken support for Kyiv. Moscow reportedly seeks control over the entire Donetsk region and aims for a more advantageous position by spring.

item.title: Serbian President Urges Companies to Invest in Uzbekistan's Growing Economy
item.description: Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić encouraged Serbian companies to increase their presence in Uzbekistan's market, focusing on joint projects in technology, industry, energy, AI, biotech, and mining. He highlighted Uzbekistan's rapid development and potential for mutual benefit, noting the country is in a period of significant growth.

item.title: US Destroys Five Iranian Tankers; Iran Responds with Missile Strikes on Jordanian Bases
item.description: The US military destroyed five Iranian oil tankers after the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) attacked a US warship twice. In response, Iran launched missile strikes on US military facilities in Jordan, targeting bases used by American forces. Jordan reported intercepting most of the missiles, with no casualties reported.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces Tax Benefits for Properties Transferred to Banks Due to Debt
item.description: Uzbekistan will provide tax benefits for properties transferred to banks due to debt. State-owned banks are permitted to sell these properties at market value through direct sales, installment plans, leasing, or other legal transactions. This aims to facilitate the resolution of debt-related property transfers.

item.title: World Leaders Congratulate Emomali Rahmon on Tajikistan's Independence Day
item.description: Leaders from various countries and international organizations sent congratulatory messages to Tajik President Emomali Rahmon on the 35th anniversary of Tajikistan's Independence Day. Messages acknowledged the country's achievements, bilateral relations, and contributions to regional cooperation, wishing peace and prosperity.

item.title: US Authorities Revealed False Information on Air Quality After 9/11 Attacks
item.description: New York authorities have released data showing elevated levels of asbestos and carcinogens in the air for months following the 9/11 attacks. The information indicates the public was misled about the air quality in the aftermath of the terrorist incidents.

item.title: Tashkent BYD Driver Fined and Vehicle Impounded for Failing to Yield to Ambulance
item.description: A BYD driver in Tashkent has been held accountable for not yielding to an ambulance. An administrative report was filed, and the vehicle was temporarily impounded. The driver explained the situation, stating it was unintentional due to music and closed windows.

item.title: Tashkent Driver Penalized for Blocking Ambulance Path
item.description: A BYD driver in Tashkent has been penalized for obstructing an ambulance's movement, following a viral video of the incident. The driver, who claimed not to have heard the ambulance due to music and closed windows, had an administrative report filed against him and his car impounded.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan aims to achieve 100% food self-sufficiency by 2030
item.description: Kyrgyzstan aims to reduce food import dependence by 2030, targeting 100% domestic self-sufficiency in key products. While domestic production meets most needs for potatoes, vegetables, and dairy, shortfalls exist in meat, eggs, sugar, oil, grains, and fruits. Efforts will focus on increasing production in these areas.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan targets 100% food self-sufficiency by 2030
item.description: Kyrgyzstan aims to reduce food import dependence by 2030, targeting 100% domestic self-sufficiency in key products. The Ministry of Agriculture reported increased domestic production for potatoes, vegetables, and dairy. Efforts will focus on boosting output for meat, eggs, sugar, oil, grains, and fruits, alongside improving storage and processing infrastructure.

item.title: Kyrgyzpharmatsiya Agrees Drug Supply Terms with Uzbek Companies
item.description: The state enterprise Kyrgyzpharmatsiya held negotiations with leading pharmaceutical manufacturers during a working trip to Uzbekistan. The focus was on practical issues for expanding cooperation and organizing direct supplies of finished pharmaceutical products. Basic parameters for future interaction were agreed upon.

item.title: 14 members of a large drug ring arrested in Tashkent, 2.5 kg of Alfa-PVP seized
item.description: Fourteen members of a large drug trafficking network have been apprehended in Tashkent, with 2.5 kg of Alfa-PVP seized. The operation disrupted an online drug store and criminal organization operating in Uzbekistan. Criminal cases have been initiated against the suspects, and pre-trial detention has been ordered.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to establish beekeeping laboratory for honey quality checks
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will open a modern beekeeping laboratory to test honey quality and compliance with international standards. The facility will address the lack of domestic testing, requiring producers to send samples abroad. This initiative aims to support the country's high-quality honey production.

item.title: UN Commission: Israel's actions in southern Syria may constitute war crimes
item.description: A UN Commission has condemned Israel's military operations and civilian detentions in southern Syria, stating these actions violate the country's sovereignty and international agreements. The commission suggests these actions could be equated to war crimes.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Water Resources Service to acquire three hybrid SUVs
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Water Resources Service plans to purchase three hybrid SUVs for 14.7 million soms. The vehicles must be new, all-wheel drive, meet Euro 5/6 emission standards, and feature advanced safety systems. Bids are accepted until September 22, 2026.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Serbia Establish Strategic Partnership, Boost Business Ties
item.description: Presidents Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Aleksandar Vučić attended a joint business forum, marking the establishment of a strategic partnership between Uzbekistan and Serbia. Over 200 business representatives participated, aiming to increase trade and industrial cooperation.

item.title: Belgrade Street Named 'Tashkent' to Symbolize Strong Uzbek-Serbian Relations
item.description: A street in Belgrade has been named 'Tashkent' during the official visit of Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev to Serbia. This naming signifies the dynamic development of bilateral relations, now elevated to a strategic partnership, and symbolizes friendship between the two nations.

item.title: Uzbekistan to participate in 200km railway construction in Serbia
item.description: Uzbekistan's builders will participate in constructing a 200-kilometer railway in Serbia. Additionally, direct flights will be launched between Tashkent and Mauritius. A person promising a governor's position for $210,000 was arrested in Fergana. Uzbekistan ranked 48th out of 91 countries in natural sciences in PISA 2025.

item.title: Uzbek President Awarded Order of the Republic of Serbia
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev received Serbia's highest state honor, the Order of the Republic of Serbia on a Grand Chain. Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić presented the award in Belgrade, recognizing Mirziyoyev's significant contribution to strengthening Uzbek-Serbian relations.

item.title: Poverty Reduction Efforts Examined in Shumanay District
item.description: A press tour in Shumanay District, Karakalpakstan, showcased efforts to reduce poverty and increase incomes. A press conference detailed measures for 2026, including creating 6,877 jobs and developing local businesses based on regional advantages, aligning with state directives.

item.title: Uzbekistan-Serbia Trade Turnover Grows Significantly
item.description: Trade and economic ties between Uzbekistan and Serbia have strengthened, with turnover increasing nearly ninefold from $1.4 million to $12 million between 2016-2025. Both nations aim to reach $50 million in mutual trade soon.

item.title: Twelve countries ban trade with Israeli settlements amid rising violence
item.description: Twelve countries, including 11 European nations and Canada, have banned trade with Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank due to rising violence. In response, Israeli officials ordered the closure of the British consulate in Jerusalem. This action follows increased tensions and violence in the region.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Serbia Establish Strategic Partnership
item.description: Uzbekistan and Serbia signed a Joint Declaration establishing a strategic partnership following talks in Belgrade. Leaders witnessed the exchange of documents on cooperation in areas including labor migration, transport, agriculture, renewable energy, and ICT.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Serbia Establish New Diplomatic Relations Phase
item.description: Uzbekistan and Serbia have entered a new phase of diplomatic relations, marked by increased political dialogue and high-level meetings. Following a summit in Tashkent, leaders signed a joint statement to expand cooperation in political, economic, and cultural spheres. Agreements were signed to strengthen economic ties and establish new consultative mechanisms.

item.title: Uzbekistan Prosecutor General's Office receives appeal to preserve historic building
item.description: Uzbekistan's Agency for Cultural Heritage has appealed to the Prosecutor General's Office to preserve a historic building at 7 Bobur Street in Tashkent. The appeal questions the legality of a 2018 decision that allocated the land for demolition and construction.

item.title: Serbia expresses readiness to cooperate with Uzbekistan on ballistic missile production
item.description: Serbia has announced its willingness to collaborate with Uzbekistan in the production of ballistic missiles. The country is already manufacturing short-range missiles and could begin producing long-range ballistic missiles within a year.

item.title: New water intake facility completed on Ak-Buura River in Osh, Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Construction of a new water intake facility has been completed on the Ak-Buura River in the Dangi section of Osh, Kyrgyzstan. The project, funded by the Asian Development Bank and the Osh mayor's office, includes a new headworks and a 2,400-meter main pipeline to supply drinking water.

item.title: Central Asia-China Political Parties Dialogue Held in Samarkand
item.description: A conference on the role of political parties in strengthening ties between Central Asia and China took place in Samarkand. The forum aimed to enhance inter-party dialogue, support interstate agreements, and achieve economic and social results. Representatives from Central Asian nations and China participated.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Armenia Discuss Bilateral Cooperation Prospects
item.description: Uzbekistan and Armenia held political consultations in Yerevan to discuss cooperation in political, trade-economic, and cultural-humanitarian spheres. Both sides expressed interest in expanding the legal framework and strengthening interaction on international platforms, focusing on industrial cooperation and transport.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan aims to export beans to Pakistan, boosting agricultural trade
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Water Resources, Agriculture, and Processing Industry met with Pakistan's Ambassador to discuss bean exports. The focus is on establishing direct links between producers and importers, participating in trade shows, and agreeing on supply volumes and terms. Kyrgyzstan's bean export potential exceeds 50,000 tons annually.
